title: ViDiHand2: Unifying Video Diffusion Priors and Hand Geometry for 3D Hand Motion Reconstruction in the Wild
whyItMatters: ViDiHand2 uses video diffusion priors and hand geometry for metric 3D hand motion reconstruction in the wild.
summary: Learning robot manipulation from egocentric human videos requires accurate metric 3D hand motion. Recent methods leverage pretrained video diffusion model (VDM) priors to recover occluded hands directly from full-frame videos, but their appearance-based depth regression generalizes poorly to unseen cameras. In this work, we propose ViDiHand2, a geometry-driven framework that reformulates VDM-based hand depth estimation from direct regression into fine-grained geometric constraint solving. whyItMatters: ToolSmith auto-generates new search tools for multimodal agents when existing tools fail on novel queries.

summary: Recent multimodal search agents use reasoning, vision, and live web search across many turns to answer questions beyond parametric knowledge by orchestrating a small library of hand-crafted search and visual tools. However, the library is laborious to create and maintain, and frozen when new query types, evidence formats, and failure modes are encountered in the wild. Human practitioners, by contrast, cope with insufficient tools by fashioning new ones from familiar parts and reusing them across tasks. Human demonstrations provide a rich source of bimanual dexterous skills, yet transferring them to robot hands remains challenging. Existing methods primarily optimize object trajectory tracking, often overlooking how human hands interact with the object. Even with accurate tracking, robots may contact incorrect object parts or slide their fingers, resulting in unstable manipulation. We present DexDuet, a framework that learns contact-preserving bimanual dexterity from a single human demonstration. whyItMatters: DexDuet learns contact-preserving bimanual dexterity from human demonstrations for robot transfer.

summary: Recently, GPT-6 Astra demonstrates strong generalization in robot control, yet limited disclosure of its training leaves open how such capabilities can be reproduced. Current MLLM methods largely focus on whether models attend to the right visual regions, implicitly treating spatial attention map as the primary key of effective visual perception. To examine this assumption, we introduce a medical VQA dataset with paired non-contrast (NC) and contrast-enhanced (CE) images that share corresponding anatomy while providing different cues. title: Polytropos: What Do Vision-Language Model Descriptions Make of a Cultural Object?
summary: Vision-language models have become a new kind of describer, writing about almost anything people see, and their descriptions now shape how cultures are known by people and by other models. Descriptions of cultures tend to turn particular things into types, and what a description loses shows what its describer lacks. summary: Most LLM agent frameworks build a crew that runs a task and exits. title: ApexID: Hierarchical Learning for Multi-Species Animal Re-Identification
whyItMatters: ApexID introduces hierarchical loss for multi-species animal re-identification across 132K images.
summary: Animal re-identification (Re-ID) must distinguish individuals across species and capture conditions. summary: Multimodal foundation models can play video games well when the game waits for them, but often fail when it keeps running. title: MomentMem: Memorizing Key Moments for Robot Manipulation

summary: Robotic manipulation often requires remembering visual information that is no longer observable, such as the original location of an object. We study visual moment memory, the ability to retain such details from key moments for subsequent manipulation. title: DiLE: Discrimination-Aware Latent-Space Learning for Universal Multimodal Embeddings
summary: Multimodal large language models have greatly improved input understanding in universal multimodal embedding models.
